title: Great Club
snippet:
Great Club -  Dark Souls - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : The Great Club is a bigger version of the Large Club, having higher base damage, but with more weight and causing no poison build up.

With high staggering power, good Guard Break and high damage, the Great Club is a powerful weapon in the right hands. Its main flaws are the slowness and clumsiness of its strikes. An adversary that can fast roll can easily roll "into" the attack of the Great Club and counterattack, thus, fat rolling or over burdening isn't wise should a Great Club be equipped.

The Great Club has incredibly high damage for its weight; out-damaging weapons nearly twice as heavy as it. Its Physical Attack Rating and practical damage are only slightly surpassed by the Demon's Greataxe, which weighs 10 more units than the Great Club for a negligible damage increase.

snippet:
Great Hammers -  Dark Souls - weapon - overview 
 overview : All Great Hammers are Strike-type weapons. They are among the largest weapons, and so their attacks are extremely powerful, but slow. This also means that they produce large amounts of damage and have good staggering power. They are designed for single powerful hits, not quick combos. Their high starting and ending lag can make great hammers tricky to use against nimble opponents. Great Hammers usually need to be wielded with both hands, as they have very high Strength requirements.

title: Ultra Greatswords
snippet:
The amount of recovery each attack with this weapon has means that your opponent is all but guaranteed a free hit if your blow does not connect. The style of these weapons, however, is to ensure that if your one big attack does connect, it does lethal amounts of damage. The sheer size and length of these weapons also gives a great attack range and their high powered strikes also inflict a lot of stun and interrupt characters with high poise. The heavy stun rate of these weapons also make it possible to *stun lock* enemies. Ultra Greatswords also have a large radius swing, making enemy players who aim for backstabs easier to handle in medium range.

Below is a list of all the Ultra Greatswords and their base stats in *Dark Souls*. Clicking on any of the names of the Ultra Greatswords will give you detailed information about that weapon on a separate page.

title: Ultra Greatswords
snippet:
Ultra Greatswords -  Dark Souls - weapon - overview 
 overview : Ultra Greatswords, as their name suggests, are the biggest, heaviest, and quite often, strongest type of sword you can acquire in the game. These massive blades all require tremendous strength to wield, and are usually best held with both hands to stagger enemies more easily. Your entire body weight is put behind each of the large swings, and while that does increase their damage potential significantly, it also means that it can consume a lot of your stamina and any miss can be extremely costly.

title: Zweihander
snippet:
Zweihander -  Dark Souls - weapon - trivia 
 trivia : The Zweihänder, a relatively modern term for a *Bidenhänder*, is a Germanic greatsword originating in the renaissance. Its name in German literally translates to "two-hander", referencing the fact that its great weight and length require it to be wielded with both hands.
The length below the two appendages (the *parierhaken*) above the crossguard is a blunt part of the blade known as the *ricasso*, which can be held and serves to shorten the wielders grip. This technique is known as half-swording, and provides better control and leverage when fighting in close quarters.
**The aforementioned appendages are designed to deflect blades away from the hand of anyone using this technique.

title: Zweihander
snippet:
Zweihander -  Dark Souls - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : The Zweihander's strong attack is its signature overhead swing. It doesn't deal quite as much damage as the strong attacks of other Ultra weapons, but deals immense poise damage like all weapons in the UGS class, but is slightly faster to swing (the other weapons require a "charge up"). Normal enemies will be immediately smashed into the ground, and almost all bigger enemies will be interrupted. It is one of the only moves in the game that can swing faster than a Mushroom Parent or Crystal Golem can attack, yet is guaranteed to break their poise, interrupting their attack. This makes it an ideal weapon/attack versus those enemies. Like most weapons with large poise-breaking capacities, barely missing an enemy with the strong attack can still cause a stagger.

title: Zweihander
snippet:
Contrary to popular belief, Zweihander is NOT a "Strength Weapon" but is a "Quality" Scaling weapon meaning it scales near equally off Strength and Dexterity and will be at its full potential at the relevant stat softcaps.

The overhead swing also has the advantage of a high vertical reach. This makes it a very good weapon to use to cut Dragon tails: most other Ultra Greatswords will require a running attack to swing upwards, and Great Hammers don't reach quite as high. The overhead swing also makes the player dodge certain attacks that reach horizontally.

The Zweihander can be a very strong weapon early in the game due to its close proximity to the starting area and relatively low stat requirement of 16 Strength to two-hand the weapon. Even un-upgraded, its base damage and staggering abilities are formidable for the Undead Burg area.

title: Assassin (class)
snippet:
The Assassin Set has only moderate physical defences but has good magic and fire defences, and high overall resistances against anything that isn't Bleed.

While the **Assassin** doesn't have any ranged attack, its Spook Sorcery is extremely useful for removing most non-fatal fall damage and for completely silencing footsteps for 20 seconds, allowing certain obstacles to be bypassed . Unfortunately, while the starting Sorcerer's Staff is a fairly good spell tool, if not exactly the best, it won't actually start to gain scaling from stats until Intelligence has reached at least 19, delaying a possible strengthening of the character's Sorceries.

Picking up the Soul Arrow Sorcery from the Shrine Handmaid gives a reusable ranged attack early on, while the weapon buffing Magic Weapon Sorcery can be gained in either Undead Settlement or Road of Sacrifices to add some of a Staff's spellbuff to weapon damage.

title: Assassin (class)
snippet:
Assassin (class) -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - lead 
 lead : The **Assassin** is one of the classes in *Dark Souls 3*.

It is a Dexterity-based class with decent Attunement for Weapon Arts and spells and some Intelligence for Sorceries.

An unusually long Thrusting Sword, the Estoc is also quite strong and has a rare sweeping heavy attack for hitting several or agile foes easier, at the cost of not having an increased critical modifier for Ripostes and Backstabs. Additionally, its Weapon Art, Shield Splitter, helps with its bad damage to the stamina of blocking targets by partially bypassing the defences of the block instead.

Its Targeting Shield, while not very suitable for blocking, is one of the game's three parrying shields and as such its Parry starts slightly earlier yet ends as late as the regular parry.

The Assassin Set has only moderate physical defences but has good magic and fire defences, and high overall resistances against anything that isn't Bleed.

title: Assassin (class)
snippet:
Assassin (class) -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - trivia 
 trivia : This class is fairly popular amongst speedrunners thanks to Spook making it possible to easier skip foes and falls.
While the Assassin doesn't have any direct equivalent class in the Dark Souls series, it does bear some resemblance to the Royalty class from FromSoftware's previous game Demon's Souls, another Dexterity/Intelligence-based class wielding a thrusting sword (in that case a Rapier) and a small shield while also providing access to a Sorcery-like spell (though in the Royalty's case it is the offensive Soul Arrow, not a self-buffing spell).

Their movesets primarily consist of horizontal slashes when one-handed and vertical slashes when two-handed.

title: Bandit (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Bandit (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - lead 
 lead : The **Bandit** is one of the classes in *Dark Souls 2*.

It has high Dexterity and well above average Faith, meaning it lends itself rather well towards builds focused either on both or only the former (though it will have strong competition from the Swordsman when it comes to pure Dexterity builds). It is rather unsuitable to spells, even the Miracle ones, due to its extremely low Attunement and Intelligence.

Bandits are actually unable to speak to Straid of Olaphis by default, the only class that can't do that, due to its extremely low Intelligence not meeting his minimum required amount of 3.

title: Bandit (Dark Souls II)
snippet: There is a curious disadvantage to its high Vitality, higher than any other starting class: when using the Third Dragon Ring, it cannot receive the full benefit of the Flynn's Ring and will get a light decrease of 4 Attack Rating compared to any other class.

title: Bandit (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Until an unlimited source of arrows is acquired, they are best either saved for trying to pull individual enemies from groups or ambushes, or for trying to kill one of the early Ogres (either the one outside the Firekeeper's Hut in Things Betwixt at the start of the tutorial that also holds the Stone Ring, or the Scholar of the First Sin-exclusive one on the way towards the Forest of Fallen Giants) for a large amount of extra Souls.

The class's Bandit Set is actually fairly good, as it has somewhat high physical defences and is, together with the Knight's partial Falconer Set, the only starting set with decent starting Poise.

Due to its very low Adaptability and Attunement it has a substandard roll (only 7 i-frames, compared to most other classes having 8 or 9 i-frames) and needs 3 points in Adaptability or 9 points in Attunement to improve this to 8 i-frames.

title: Bandit (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Bandits are actually unable to speak to Straid of Olaphis by default, the only class that can't do that, due to its extremely low Intelligence not meeting his minimum required amount of 3.

The starting weapons are somewhat mixed, with the Short Bow following the higher starting value in Dexterity while the Hand Axe instead focuses on Strength. The Hand Axe is most likely better replaced with an actually Dexterity-focused weapon, though those are in limited supply until Blacksmith Lenigrast's shop is opened, mostly the Dagger in Things Betwixt and the Halberd in the Forest of Fallen Giants. Beyond extra weapons such as the Spear and the Rapier, Lenigrast also holds the game's first infinite supply of ammunition (merely more Wood Arrows, but still) and another Short Bow.

 lead : **Bows** are a type of weapons in *Dark Souls III*. Bows are a ranged weapon type that requires a modest investment in Strength and a moderate investment in Dexterity. Bows can be equipped in either the left or right hand weapon slots. Because the player is required to hold the bow with both hands to fire, the Strength requirement can be circumvented.

All bows have a "zoom" feature that allows the player to get a closer look at their aim point. It should be noted that different types of Arrows have different ranges that add to a specific bow's range. This affects the accuracy of the projectile resulting in some shots seeming inaccurate (this does not affect locked-on shots). Range can also be increased by equipping the Hawk Ring.

 overview : As the name states, this weapon was intended to be connected to Marvelous Chester in the Royal Wood, either as a dropped weapon, or as a gift to the player. However, as it was cut from the final release of the game, it is unknown how the player would have obtained it.

Due to its nature as cut content, Chester's Black Zweihander is simply a texture in the game files. This means that even if the player modified their save file, it would not have its own stats anyway, as an existing weapon's model has to be overridden in order to 'obtain' it. title: Cleric (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Cleric (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - lead 
 lead : The **Cleric** is one of the classes in *Dark Souls 3*.

It is a Faith-focused class, with decent Attunement, Strength, and Luck. This makes them well-suited to a Miracle-heavy build, and to using the many Lightning-attuned weapons as they are often also have good Strength-scaling.

While it does indeed have spells, in the form of Heal (which heals) and Force (which throws enemies away from you), it does not have any that causes damage, with the earliest ones not being found until Cathedral of the Deep or Farron Keep. This means the class will have to focus primarily on weapons initially, and will do well to keep them upgraded as offensive Miracles consume a lot of Focus Points.

title: Cleric (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Cleric (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - trivia 
 trivia : This is the only spellcasting-focused starting class in Dark Souls 3 that doesn't have a damage-boosting ring. Presumably this is because the Cleric doesn't have a damaging Miracle equipped from the start, and the Morne's Ring can instead be found in the Road of Sacrifices.
This class has remained remarkably similar throughout the series, always carrying a Mace and the Heal Miracle.

title: Cleric (Dark Souls III)
snippet: The Cleric's Sacred Chime is a fairly good casting tool and is actually the strongest casting tool for Miracles from 45 to 49 Faith. Its Spell Buff (the stat that affects how strong scaling spells are) doesn't actually increase until at least 19 Faith has been reached. Its Weapon Art is Gentle Prayer, a regenerative effect that always restores 360 hp over the course of a minute as long as the Chime is held in an active hand (so replacing it with another item stops it, as does two-handing the item in the other hand). This effect will actually outheal the Heal Miracle by up to 20% until the Chime's Spell Buff reaches 120, and even afterwards it is a strong if slow alternative due to only having about a third the cost in Focus Points.

title: Cleric (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
The Cleric Set is a light, caster-type armor set and as such has low physical defences and high elemental defences, while also having high Poison and Curse resistances.

The first trainer for more Miracles is found in the Undead Settlement for further development.

title: Cleric (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
The Mace is an unexpectedly strong weapon for what may at first seem like a spellcasting class, but in reality it is often a **Cleric's** main armament. This is because Strike damage is often the strongest physical damage type as armored and skeletal enemies are weak to it (most other physical damage types have fewer enemies weak to them), strong Strength-scaling for easy damage increases, a fairly good moveset, and has a good Weapon Art for trading hits with opponents. How the Weapon Art works is that Perseverance adds a flat 45% extra absorption and causes the attacks of light weapons to bounce off the user, while also granting great Hyper Armor to prevent being staggered.

The Blue Wooden Shield is not very good, having only decent physical and magic defence with serviceable Stability. While it does have Parry (albeit the inferior Medium Shield version), a strong Weapon Skill shield like the early Silver Eagle Kite Shield would probably serve as a better replacement.

title: Crossbows (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Crossbows (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - weapon - lead 
 lead : **Crossbows** are a type of weapon in *Dark Souls III*.

Crossbows are a ranged weapon that have rather low Strength and Dexterity requirements and offer no scaling, making them ideal for builds that do not invest heavily into physical stats. Unlike bows and greatbows, crossbows can be held and fired in one hand, but require the player to reload between shots as indicated by an arrow head in the top portion of the weapon icon. This makes them ideal ranged weapons for engaging foes within lock-on range.

title: Crossbows (Dark Souls III)
snippet: Crossbows can be equipped in either the main hand or off hand. When two-handed, all crossbows have a "zoom" feature, activated by pressing the off-hand weak attack button (or block), that allows the player to manually aim their shots from a first-person point of view. It should be noted that different types of Bolts have varying ranges that add to a specific crossbow's range. This affects the accuracy of the projectile resulting in some shots seeming inaccurate (this does not affect locked-on shots). Range can also be increased by equipping the Hawk Ring.

 lead : The **Deprived** is one of the classes in *Dark Souls 2*.

Unlike the other classes, it doesn't start with any weapons or Lifegems and only has the unequipped Imported Set as armor. Make sure to retrieve the Dagger found in the first side path of Things Betwixt as an initial weapon, while the Morning Star in Majula can be wielded two-handed with 2 more Strength and 1 more Dexterity. A Cleric's Sacred Chime can be found near the Morning Star if wanting to use Miracles, a Shield can be gained by either buying one of Maughlin the Armorer in Majula or be found on the path to Heide's Tower of Flame, and a Sorcerer's Staff can be found behind a hidden wall in the Forest of Fallen Giants.

The low level means leveling up is slightly cheaper than for any other class, and the all-6 statline serves as a decent base for a build focused on the Mundane infusion since that scales of the lowest stat.

 soft_caps : As of the 1.32 Regulations patch, Dexterity has two soft caps: 40 and 80.

For most normal builds, the damage return for weapon attack rating stops at 40 Dexterity. This applies to both quality builds and Dexterity-focused builds.

When utilizing the Sharp infusion, scaling on weapons changes at high levels. Attack rating returns between 40 and 60 Dexterity are relatively poor, with most weapons only seeing an increase in 1 point of damage per level of investment. Dexterity increases damage done by weapons with a scaling mechanic. A letter denoting a weapon's specific scaling properties is noted beneath the weapon's required Dexterity stat. The letters range in order of effectiveness from **E**, **D**, **C**, **B**, **A**, and **S**.

Weapons with an **E** rating for scaling will receive a poor benefit from investment in Dexterity while weapons with an **S** rating receive the greatest benefit.

As is with every other stat in the game, it also has indirect bonuses such as increasing the player character's flat damage absorption. Notable among these indirect bonuses is a reduction to fall-damage with every level invested into Dexterity.

snippet:
Composite Bow (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : This bow has low range, but this is hard to notice in *Dark Souls II*. It is usually not a problem. title: Bastard Sword
snippet:
Bastard Sword -  Dark Souls - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : Bastard Sword is one of the few true Quality scaling weapons at 51% Strength and 51% Dexterity scaling, making it fitting for a 27 Strength, 40 Dexterity build. Despite its very slightly higher damage, it is typically ignored in favor of the free Claymore due to its shorter reach and lack of a thrust attack, consequently being seldom-used within the game unless the player is unaware how to acquire the Claymore.

title: Endurance (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Endurance (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - general_information 
 general_information : Increasing one's Endurance affects several attributes of the player. Endurance's main effect is to increase both the player's Stamina, as well as their total HP however, this does not increase it as much as raising Vigor will. Endurance is also interactive with Strength, Dexterity and Vitality, the sum of which determines the player's natural Physical Defense. Finally, Endurance is also interactive with the Adaptability stat, in that raising the two stats at the same rate will grant extra natural Poise.

Unlike in *Dark Souls* and *Demon's Souls*, raising Endurance does not improve a character's Equip Load.

title: Lion Greataxe
snippet:
Lion Greataxe -  Dark Souls II - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : The Lion Greataxe is a quality Strength and Dexterity-based weapon, which is uncommon for greataxes as they are often Strength-based weapons. Its base damage is poor and seems to not compete with other greataxes in terms of damage output, even on a quality build. Its only redeeming feature is its low weight for a greataxe. However, once upgraded to +3 and beyond, it gains a "B" scaling in Strength.

title: Sorcerer (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Sorcerer (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - lead 
 lead : The **Sorcerer** is one of the classes in *Dark Souls 2*.

It is an Intelligence-based class, serving as an excellent base for a build focused on Sorceries or Hexes, and also possibly for a build using a Magic infused weapon that wants to start with some spells. It has a decent starting Dexterity but a horrendous starting Strength, barely even enough to wield their weapon and even with effective Strength being doubled when two-handing so the vast majority of weapons can't be wielded without some investment, only some Daggers.

The starting Sorcerer's Staff is a decent, quick-casting spell tool for Sorceries that is worth upgrading, while the Dagger is a decent, if short reaching weapon whose poor Durability should be supplemented by picking up a second copy in the Things Betwixt tutorial.

title: Herald (class)
snippet:
Herald (class) -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - lead 
 lead : The **Herald** is one of the classes in *Dark Souls 3*.

It is a hybrid class, with a decent amount of Vigor, Strength, Dexterity, and Faith, but a slightly below average Attunement (especially for a class with a starting spell) and Endurance. It seems intended to provide the basis for a build more focused on either one of Strength or Dexterity or a mix of both, that still has the stats to carry some supportive Miracles from its Faith.

Its Spear deals somewhat mediocre damage and is quite short for a polearm, but is actually fairly quick and can attack while still keeping a block up, at the cost of lowering that block's effectiveness (meaning even a 100% block shield will let some damage slip through if hit). Its skill is Shield Splitter, a heavy thrust that partially bypasses blocking.

title: Club (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Club (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : The Club is a solid starting weapon for a strength build. It is lightweight, has low stamina cost and excellent strength scaling from base level, allowing for very respectable damage. The club is reliable throughout the game and will often serve as a go-to weapon for strength builds in situations where speed is essential and heavier weapons become impractical.

title: Parameter Bonus (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Parameter Bonus (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - lead 
 lead : **Parameter Bonus** (also known as **Scaling**) is a gameplay mechanic in *Dark Souls II* similar to the ones from the first game.

It is a rating ranging from "E" to "S" of how well a weapon synergizes with a specific stat. These stats include Strength, Dexterity, Magic (mainly Intelligence), Lightning (mainly Faith), Fire (mainly a combination of Intelligence and Faith) and Dark (lowest stat between Intelligence and Faith).

All the details are not completely known; in particular, how scaling works when there are multiple stats at once (such as for "quality" weapons).

title: Warrior (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Warrior (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - lead 
 lead : The **Warrior** is one of the classes in *Dark Souls 3*.

It is a Strength-focused class, with good Vigor for extra health and a decent amount of Endurance and Luck for more Stamina and Item Discovery. It does, however, have fairly low Dexterity and casting stats, with its very low Attunement of 6 making it notable for being the only starting class that doesn't immediately have an attunement slot for spells.

title: Refined Gem
snippet:
Refined Gem -  Dark Souls III - item - usage 
 usage : Can be used to create Refined weapons through Blacksmith Andre in Firelink Shrine.

Infusing a weapon with a Refined Gem will increase the scaling bonuses from both Strength and Dexterity, without compromising one or the other, while also equalizing their scaling. While it does also lower the weapon's base damage slightly, the improved scaling bonuses, in most cases, will result in an overall damage increase.

Refined infusions are a solid choice if a player is utilizing a quality build, where Strength and Dexterity are leveled equally. Furthermore, Refined weapons are still able to be fully buffed by resins, bundles, or spells.

title: Knight (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Knight (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - lead 
 lead : The **Knight** is one of the classes in *Dark Souls 3*.

It is the most newcomer friendly-class in Dark Souls 3, thanks to its strong and versatile weapon, its 100%-physical block shield, its strong armor, and its well-rounded stats. It is also suitable to a wide variety of builds thanks to its good Strength and Dexterity, and decent Intelligence and Faith. It also has good Vitality, letting it carry heavier equipment easier.

The Long Sword is a strong and versatile weapon, with fast swings on its light attacks and a strong thrusting attack as its one-handed heavy attack, capable of dealing heavy damage if a Counter Attack is landed. Its Weapon Art, Stance, is similarly versatile, as following as using a light attack while holding the stance leads to a block-breaking uppercut while the heavy attack version is a lunging thrust to catch enemies off guard.

title: Swordsman
snippet:
Swordsman -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - lead 
 lead : The **Swordsman** is one of the classes in *Dark Souls 2*.

It has the highest Dexterity of the starting classes, making it a good base for a build focused on that stat, such as one using Curved Swords and Bows. Additionally, a decent base Attunement and Intelligence makes using support Sorceries such as Magic Weapon easier.

The starting weapons this class wields are the only ones that are upgraded (though only to +1) and are compatible with each other for the purpose of Power Stancing, though another 2 points in Strength and 8 points in Dexterity are needed for that. Instead, it may be easier to either focus on one of the weapons as the main weapon, with perhaps a shield from Maughlin the Armorer in the other hand, or to get a second Shortsword from the Forest of Fallen Giants as that only requires the 2 extra points in Strength to begin Power Stancing.

title: Large Club (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Large Club (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : The Large Club is slightly larger than a Greatsword, and slightly smaller than the Great Club. It features vertical overhead attacks, and a few sweeping attacks. It has multiple bumps around the end of the weapon.

The Large Club has an overall identical moveset and attack speed as the Great Club. While it does have a lower base damage, it does boast an A scaling in strength, which can be upgraded to an S scaling, making this a viable choice for a strength build.

title: Benhart's Parma
snippet:
Benhart's Parma -  Dark Souls II - shield - characteristics 
 characteristics : Benhart's Parma has a very high resistance to Magic, second only to the Magic Shield. Its other elemental defenses and resistances are average, as well as its stability and durability. However, the Strength requirement is fairly low, making it a suitable choice for players without much Strength or Vitality.

Overall, it is a relatively-balanced, lightweight shield, but some other small shields will still outperform it in specific scenarios.

title: Greatshields (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Greatshields (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - shield - lead 
 lead : **Greatshields** are a type of shield in *Dark Souls III*.

Greatshields are characterized by their immense weight, high Strength requirement, and extremely strong defenses. Because of their high weight, most greatshields will require the wielder to invest not only in Strength, but also Vitality, as well as Endurance to fortify their stamina pool. However, properly wielded, a greatshield will easily protect the player from most forms of damage from all but the strongest of foes. Greatshields are incapable of performing parries, and instead allow the wielder to Shield Bash their foes, or perform the Weapon Skill of their right-hand weapon without having to two-hand it.

Because of their innately high stability, upgrading a greatshield is crucial, as increasing their already strong stability will allow them to virtually ignore the stamina damage dealt by smaller weapons.

title: Uchigatana (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Uchigatana (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : Very similar to the Uchigatana of Dark Souls in terms of moveset, the One-Handed Heavy Attack has a very wide range, making this weapon very useful for attack/withdrawal situations.

The Uchigatana can prove to be a solid, reliable weapon for Dexterity centered builds throughout the whole course of the game. Requiring only 10 Strength, and 16 Dexterity, the Uchigatana has the lowest requirements of all available katanas in Dark Souls II. With a weight of only 5.0 units, it is the second lightest katana, the lightest being Darkdrift.

title: Thief
snippet:
Thief -  Dark Souls - mechanic - lead 
 lead : The **Thief** is a class in *Dark Souls*.

Thieves are one of the more difficult classes to start as, with low Vitality, Strength and Endurance stats that force them to use evasive maneuvers and deliver critical hits with their Bandit's Knife. Their equipment makes them rely on backstabs and parrying to defeat enemies, with their Target Shield giving a longer parry window.

Thieves come equipped with a Master Key, so they are able to open up basic locked doors. This may, however, do more harm than good for new players, as it can cause them to become more easily lost.

title: Magic (upgrade path)
snippet:
Magic (upgrade path) -  Dark Souls - mechanic - overview 
 overview : By upgrading a weapon down the Magic upgrade path, it gains increased Magic Damage scaling through Intelligence, while also losing Physical Damage through Strength and Dexterity scaling. This makes the Magic path suitable for those with a high Intelligence stat, but low Strength and Dexterity stats.

A standard weapon with a magical weapon augmentation, such as Crystal Magic Weapon, deals more damage than Magic weapons in almost every instance; however, Magic weapons have the advantage of being permanent and not having to be buffed.

The Enchanted upgrade path offers even better scaling with Intelligence than the Magic path, albeit at the cost of even heavier Strength and Dexterity bonus reductions.

title: Gargoyle Flame Hammer
snippet:
Gargoyle Flame Hammer -  Dark Souls III - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : Scales best with Strength but the fairly high base fire damage means it works fairly well on a pyromancer (Intelligence/Faith) build with only moderate amounts of Strength.

title: Dexterity (Dark Souls)
snippet:
Dexterity (Dark Souls) -  Dark Souls - mechanic - general_information 
 general_information : Dexterity is used to meet requirements and increase damage to weapons that scale well with Dexterity. Dexterity softcaps at **20/40/45**. You will want to stop at 20 and 40 overall for physical attack and 45 for the spell cast speed of some spells. This spell cast speed increase is generally unimportant for a PvE caster build, but worth noting if you happen to get into PvP.

Unlike Strength there is no boost to Dexterity when two handing, though players will still gain increased damage in practice when two handing due to the Motion Value modifier.

title: Black Blade
snippet:
Black Blade -  Dark Souls III - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : The Black Blade is a katana with some simple trade-offs that lets it stand out as a unique weapon within its class. Its primary draw is its high damage, a Sharp-infused Black Blade being one of the highest damage katanas available for a Dexterity-focused build, but it is somewhat short and heavy, and has a hefty strength requirement of 18 that may make it inaccessible for some builds.

title: Parameter Bonus (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Parameter Bonus (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - soft_caps 
 soft_caps : In terms of "return on investment" (for strength and scaling), unlike in *Dark Souls*, players get the "best" return on investment in the 30~40 range. The gains go something like this:
0~30 : 100%
30~40 : 150%
40~50 : 50%
50~60 : 25%
Where "100%" represents an arbitrary scale of what the player would get per point for a given rating.

In terms of scaling, it means the best gains are for "putting all your eggs in the same basket", with either "40/20" for Strength/quality or "20/40" for Dexterity, but never "30/30".
